# Native REAPER 7.86 grammar fixture

`native-probe.rpp` and `native-settings.txt` are unmodified files from the independently generated native probe in [Actions run 44514197389](https://github.com/djshellshoxxx/websoundedit/actions/runs/44514197389), job `135525836904`, artifact `14524629673`, head `b3b7f585e17ac0d8dee27cb1b4cd42c676410778`.

REAPER reported `7.86/linux-x86_64`. The private native session completed its Lua script with `OK`, exited with code 0 and no signal, and did not time out. The official archive SHA-256 was `c2f9d8616bd1dc6175993b82451e1c6e352c6761e7ae6d72400a3f3dfb03bedb`.

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| native-probe.rpp | `2b507f24e137aff0be644c84751e9f0cfb5e80cd0a5f667dd01c46990f85e35e` |
| native-settings.txt | `a5238aa69ef37237f5ac8e0129cd4285a749fcbe8730a8b373b1f02de5141e42` |

The probe's source WAV files were generated by the standalone encoder in `scripts/probe-reaper.mjs`; they are reproducible and are not needed for the text fixture. The regression supplies independent local PCM under their exact aliases.

This first probe changed project tempo after inserting beat-attached items. The saved project therefore contains take playback rate `1.06666666666667` and adjusted timing. The unmodified file must be rejected as unsupported stretching. A clearly derived test changes only that take rate to 1 to exercise native defaults, channel counts, visible trims and metadata without claiming that the derived file was written by REAPER. Subsequent native harness setup sets tempo before adding items.

The fixture establishes native grammar and settings. Full rendered-audio compatibility is asserted separately by `scripts/verify-reaper.mjs`.
